references.text: The Levites are appointed to take care of the tabernacle and all its utensils, which directly relates to their responsibility for the equipment of the tent of meeting.
The specific duties of the Gershonites regarding the coverings and curtains of the tent of meeting clarify what utensils the Levites were to guard.
The Kohathites' responsibility for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the holy utensils specifies what is meant by the equipment of the tent of meeting.
The Merarites' task with the boards, pillars, and sockets of the tabernacle shows the practical service rendered at the tabernacle.
The Kohathites were to carry the holy objects after Aaron and his sons had covered them, demonstrating the Levites' service for the people of Israel.
The service of the Levites at the tabernacle and their responsibility to assist the priests is further explained here as a lasting arrangement.
Aaron and his sons were to tend the lamps in the tent of meeting, which is part of the service that the Levites were to support.
The overview of the tabernacle's equipment under the supervision of the Levites through Ithamar shows their administrative responsibility.
The service of the Levites at the house of the Lord during David's time included taking care of the courtyards, rooms, and all holy utensils, continuing the tasks from the wilderness period.
The Levites were appointed to their service at the temple according to David's arrangement, extending the tabernacle service.
